rationale:
Adds a read-only reachability instrument over the retained tree and corrects one stale declaration comment; no routing, dispatch order, or public signature moves.

The slice is touched at exactly one file, core/view/include/pulp/view/pointer_dispatch.hpp, and the edit there is a COMMENT. dispatch_context_menu's doc still read 'Only the hit view is consulted -- the callback does not bubble to ancestors', which 20260913-context-menu-arming-and-bubbling made false: the implementation now walks target-to-root and fires the first view carrying a callback. The declaration, its overload set, and its behaviour are unchanged; only the sentence describing them is. This matters more than a typo fix because the header is the contract a tool author reads: the press-reach instrument added in this same change was first written against the header's claim and had to be rewritten against the code, which is exactly the failure mode a stale contract produces.

Everything else in this change is additive and outside the slice: a new public header and translation unit (core/view/{include/pulp/view,src}/press_reach.{hpp,cpp}) providing reach_of_press, rect_in_root and audit_press_reach, plus View::simulate_context_click declared in view.hpp and defined in press_reach.cpp.

reach_of_press RESOLVES without delivering: it calls View::hit_test and then reproduces the dispatch's own handler walk, and runs no callback, dismisses no overlay and moves no state. It therefore cannot perturb the tree it measures, which is what makes it usable as a gate rather than as an integration test. It deliberately reproduces the existing walk rather than defining a second one: both channels bubble from the hit view to the root and the first listener wins, which is dispatch_context_menu's walk for the right button and deliver_mouse_down's for the left. An instrument that invented a third rule would answer about a dispatch that does not exist.

rect_in_root composes a view's root-space rect by summing bounds and subtracting every ScrollView ancestor's scroll, then VERIFIES the result by round-tripping the rect's centre through point_to_local -- the same function the hosts route real presses through -- and returns std::nullopt when a set_scale or transform matrix on the path makes the additive walk wrong. audit_press_reach presses every control advertising a handler at the centre of its own painted rect and reports a census beside its findings, because a clean audit over zero examined targets is a blind run and the two are otherwise indistinguishable.

View::simulate_context_click delegates to route_context_press so there is one policy rather than two; it exists because simulate_click with button = right delivers through the ordinary mouse channels and opens no menu, and nothing about that overload's name says so.

Nothing about left-button routing, capture, focus, wheel, scroll, gesture arbitration, or the down/drag/up contracts changed, and no host branches differently. This is Pulp-only. The defect class it exists to catch -- an intermediate node with a zero-area box sealing off a subtree of correctly sized, correctly wired controls, survivable only through hit_test's symmetric ~500px overflow slack -- is an artifact of a retained tree whose hit region is derived per-node from bounds with a slack rule layered on top; a Vellum-native retained UI kernel should make a control's reachable region a first-class, inspectable property rather than something a tool has to rediscover by pressing. There is no named immutable Vellum framework commit being backported here, and this records no Vellum acknowledgement.
